theme: Encoding numbers that are mostly small
title: Predictable Codec: Bit-Width Blocks Under a Branch Tax
strategies: trivial: one block, the checker's own minimal-width whole-stream construction (reproduces baseline B, ~0.1)
greedy: fixed-size sqrt(N) chunks, per-chunk minimal width -- the textbook bit-packing recipe; ignores the misprediction tax entirely, so it thrashes between widths on regime-changing streams

strong: quantize the width alphabet to a small palette fit to the data's own bit-length distribution (1-D k-means over k=1..5 candidates), then greedily extend maximal same-width runs and DP-chain them -- trades a few wasted bits per block for a branch-free (or nearly transition-free) decode
headroom above strong: a true exact DP over all block boundaries and all 0..30 widths jointly (not just k-means-derived palettes), or adapting the palette locally instead of globally
